$comment: U6: every copper edit made by hand to the four flagged signal-integrity groups,
in the order applied. This is a LOG, not a replay script -- the QSPI bus was
re-routed by KiCadRoutingTools between the 'qspi-strip' and 'crystal' steps:
python route.py in.kicad_pcb out.kicad_pcb \
--nets /QSPI_CLK /QSPI_NCS /QSPI_IO0 /QSPI_IO1 /QSPI_IO2 /QSPI_IO3 \
--layers F.Cu In1.Cu In2.Cu B.Cu --layer-costs 20 -1 -1 1.0 \
--track-width 0.254 --via-size 0.6 --via-drill 0.3 \
--no-fix-drc-settings --overwrite
The negative layer costs are load-bearing: they make In1/In2 obstacle-only, so
the router keeps signal copper out of the two plane layers AND still treats
their copper as something a via must clear. Under Git Bash, export
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 first or every /NET argument is rewritten into a Windows path
and the router silently reports 'no valid nets to route'.
Re-applying these steps to the HEAD board will NOT reproduce the result on its
own. They are here so every hand-placed coordinate is reviewable as text.
U6 CAN group (R9).
CAN1_H: the 2-via bottom hop between the pair lane and U8.7 avoids nothing --
the top corridor x177-186 / y126-135 is empty except the +3V3 run at y=128.095.
Replaced with one straight top segment. 2 vias -> 0, matching CAN1_L.
CAN2_H: the H3.1->P2.1 jumper stub ran 8.53 mm THROUGH the Inner2 +5V plane.
Both endpoints are PTH pads, so the same path on the Bottom layer costs zero
vias and cuts no plane. The remaining single via at (122.460,132.953) is a
FORCED crossing -- U9's pin order (H south of L) is opposite P2's (H on the
near pin), and the north band is occupied by CAN2_RX (y=127.333) and CAN2_TX
(y=128.531), so L cannot detour. One via is the minimum, not a defect.
U6 CAN1, second pass. Removing CAN1_H's via hop exposed why it existed:
CAN1_L's termination branch (R14.2 -> P1.2) runs the south lane and then
LOOPS east and back north-west into P1.2, enclosing the pocket H had to
escape from. With the loop in place any top-layer H route crosses it.
Fix the topology instead of dodging it: give L's termination branch the free
north corridor (y=128.6, between the +3V3 run at 128.095 and P1's pads at
129.0 -- verified empty from x166.5 to 179), leaving the south lane to H
alone. Then H runs P1.1 -> lane -> U8.7 with no crossing and no vias, and
L runs U8.6 -> P1.2 -> north corridor -> R14.2, also with none.
Note what this does NOT claim: H and L are not a coupled pair between U8 and
P1. They sit on opposite sides of the terminal block because H lands on the
far pin, and no routing fixes that -- only moving parts would.
U6 USB, third pass. Pass 2 put via A at x=37.100, which shorted the Inner1
VBUS run at x=36.852 -- a reminder that a through via is checked against ALL
four layers, not the two you are routing on. Clearing that trace requires
Both vias move east to x >= 37.42, still on DM's original 45-degree approach,
so the path length and the 0.390 mm pair skew are unchanged.
The bottom excursion is 0.76 mm against DP's 1.68 mm: the via count and layer
set match exactly, the excursion length does not, because the Inner1 VBUS run
and D9.3's pad bracket the diagonal and leave only 0.8 mm of usable travel.
U6 QSPI: strip the six bus members whole so the bus can be re-routed
onto one layer. QSPI_CLK_MCU (the R9->U1.51 stub) is deliberately kept.
U6 crystal (R6). OSC_OUT could not be single-layer at the imported placement:
X1's ground pad X1.4 sits 0.243 mm east of U1's pad wall, and the MCU's 0.5 mm
pad pitch leaves 0.22 mm between pads -- both below the 0.457 mm a 0.254 track
needs. Every escape from U1.26 was therefore a via, which is why the import ran
5.3 mm of OSC_OUT on the bottom layer.
That bottom run is the worst place it could be: the Inner2 keepout voids the
+5V plane over exactly this region, so the nearest reference to those 5.3 mm is
Inner1, 1.28 mm away -- roughly six times the loop height of a top-layer route
over the same plane. On an oscillator that is the one net where it matters.
Moving X1 0.5 mm east opens a 0.743 mm corridor, enough to escape U1.26 north
and run the whole net on the top layer 0.21 mm above solid Inner1 GND. East was
blocked until this unit rerouted QSPI off its three vias at x=166.6-166.8; with
those gone the only thing in the way is the crystal's own case-ground trace,
re-authored here to run down x=166.45 instead of x=165.959.
U6 crystal, correction. The C42 leg ran from X1.3's pad north-east and passed
0.178 mm from the surviving GND stub at (166.213..166.721, 104.856) -- closer
than the two half-widths, so the copper actually touched (DRC: shorting_items).
Tap the load cap off the trunk at (165.400,104.450) instead, which keeps 0.51 mm
to that stub and puts C42 0.7 mm from the T rather than 1.9 mm around the pad.
